findings.title: parseBody after c.req.formData() fails or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts), short-circuit before reading bytes when a FormData is already cached, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`, and only fall through to `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData()` otherwise. Add a regression test in src/request.test.ts for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies. Alternative, if the byte round-trip is not needed: revert the line to `await (request as Request).formData()`; the mixed-case skip was caused by the gate in parseBody, and native `Request.formData()` parsed `Multipart/Form-Data` correctly on Node 24.21.0 in the probe (assumption: other supported runtimes are equally case-insensitive, which was not verified here).
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()

residual_risks: Mixed-case handling was only exercised on Node 24.21.0, where native `Request.formData()` already parses `Multipart/Form-Data` case-insensitively. `c.req.formData()` still goes through the native path with the un-normalized header (src/request.ts:238), so a runtime whose native parser is case-sensitive would still fail there; this could not be checked in this environment.

Callsite completeness is grep-only: non-test callers of parseBody/bufferToFormData inside src are src/request.ts:217 and src/validator/validator.ts:120. `parseBody` is also a public export (hono/utils/body), and it now consumes a raw Request via `arrayBuffer()` instead of `formData()`; external callers that pass Request-like objects or stub `formData()` (as the removed test spy did) are not visible from this repository.
testing_gaps: No test covers `c.req.formData()` followed by `c.req.parseBody()` on a HonoRequest (multipart and urlencoded); src/request.test.ts passes at head (38/38) because it only checks parseBody() followed by other body readers, so the regression above is unguarded.

The new mixed-case parseBody tests in src/utils/body.test.ts use raw `Request` objects only, so the new HonoRequest branch that writes `bodyCache.formData` (src/utils/body.ts:128-131) has no mixed-case coverage and no assertion on what a subsequent `c.req.formData()` / `c.req.text()` returns.

findings.title: parseBody() after c.req.formData() regresses; no test covers it
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), reuse an already-cached FormData before touching the ArrayBuffer path, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`. Smallest-diff alternative: restore `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` and keep only the new `mediaType` gate in `parseBody` -- a scratch mutant doing that passes the inputs of both new body.test.ts cases on Node 24, because native `Request.formData()` already matches the media type case-insensitively (assumption: other supported runtimes follow the Fetch spec here). Either way add regression tests to the `req.parseBody()` block in src/request.test.ts for multipart and urlencoded bodies: `await req.formData(); expect(await req.parseBody()).toEqual({ foo: 'bar' })`.

findings.title: New bodyCache.formData seeding in parseFormData is untested
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the `req.parseBody()` describe block in src/request.test.ts, for both a multipart and an urlencoded HonoRequest: `expect(await req.parseBody()).toEqual({ foo: 'bar' }); expect((await req.formData()).get('foo')).toBe('bar')`. Optionally also assert `await req.text()` equals the original urlencoded payload to pin the new arrayBuffer-first cache order.

findings.title: New bufferToFormData test passes without the buffer.ts change
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether the normalization in src/utils/buffer.ts is needed for a supported runtime. If it is, cover it where it is observable (a runtime-tests suite for that runtime); if it is not, drop the `contentType.replace(...)` line and rename this test to what it really pins, e.g. 'Should keep a mixed-case boundary intact'.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/buffer.test.ts:126-131 -- const result = await bufferToFormData(
      arrayBuffer,
      'Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=sampleBoundary'
    )

    expect(result.get('test')).toBe('Hello')

residual_risks: The claim that native formData() is already case-insensitive was executed only on Node v24.21.0 (undici). Bun, Deno, workerd, Fastly and Lambda runtimes were not available offline, so whether the parseFormData rewrite or the buffer.ts normalization is required on any of them is unverified; the Fetch spec's MIME-type extraction lowercases the essence, which is the assumption behind the 'revert to request.formData()' alternative.

parseBody() no longer calls `request.formData()` at all (the PR had to delete the `vi.spyOn(req, 'formData')` mock in src/utils/body.test.ts for that reason). Request-like objects from adapters or user code that override `formData()` but not `arrayBuffer()` are now bypassed; callsite completeness for such objects is grep-only and limited to this repository.

The body cache now holds `arrayBuffer` first and `formData` second after parseBody(). Probed sequences (parseBody twice, text()/blob() then parseBody, parseBody then text()/formData()/cloneRawRequest) behave the same or better than base, but other orderings and the body-limit middleware's wrapped request were not probed.
testing_gaps: Behavior the rewrite changed for the better is unpinned: at base `c.req.text()` then `c.req.parseBody()` threw a TypeError and `parseBody()` then `cloneRawRequest()` produced an unparseable (multipart) or garbage (urlencoded) body; both now work at head but no test asserts it, so the improvement can silently revert together with any fix for the formData()-first regression.

No test for a media type followed by whitespace before the parameter separator (e.g. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded ; charset=UTF-8`), the only input that exercises the new `.trim()` in parseBody's media-type normalization. It works at both base and head.

No HonoRequest-level (c.req.parseBody()) test with a mixed-case Content-Type; the two new body.test.ts cases pass plain `Request` objects, so the `request instanceof HonoRequest` branches of the fix are only reached with lower-case media types. Probed manually at head: works.

findings.title: parseBody() after formData() reparses reserialized body, injecting fields (CWE-436)
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), short-circuit on an existing cache entry before reading the buffer, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`. Add tests for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both urlencoded and multipart bodies.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: parseBody() now decides with `split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()`, and String.prototype.trim strips characters (U+00A0, \f, \v) that Headers and the CSRF middleware regex (`/^\b(application\/x-www-form-urlencoded|multipart\/form-data|text\/plain)\b/i`) do not. With `Content-Type: \u00a0application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and a cross-site Origin, csrf() lets the request through and parseBody() now attempts to parse it. On Node 24 the runtime MIME parser rejects it (TypeError -> 500 instead of the previous `{}`), so there is no bypass there; whether Bun, Deno or workerd `Response.formData()` are equally strict was not verifiable offline.

findings.title: parseBody now buffers and retains the raw body alongside FormData
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData`, restore `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` and drop the `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData` + manual `bodyCache.formData` assignment; keep the new case-insensitive `mediaType` gate in `parseBody`. For a `HonoRequest` this goes through `#cachedBody('formData')`, which already caches the result. Assumption: target runtimes' native `formData()` parse the MIME type case-insensitively as the Fetch spec requires (confirmed on Node 24 only, where mixed-case multipart and urlencoded both parse natively). If a supported runtime turns out to be case-sensitive, fall back to the buffered path only when the media type is not already lower-case.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()

findings.title: parseBody re-parses the body on every call, ignoring cached FormData
findings.suggested_fix: Preferred: restore `await (request as Request).formData()` in `parseFormData` (same change as the buffering finding), which reuses `bodyCache.formData` through `HonoRequest#cachedBody`. If the buffered path is kept, read the cache first, mirroring `validator.ts:115-116`: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { ...arrayBuffer + bufferToFormData, then cache... }`.

residual_risks: Memory and timing were measured on Node 24 (undici) only; Bun, Deno and workerd were not measured. The extra retained `bodyCache.arrayBuffer` copy is runtime-independent because it comes from `HonoRequest#cachedBody`, but its relative cost against each runtime's native `formData()` is unverified, as is whether those runtimes' native `formData()` accept mixed-case media types (the assumption behind the suggested fix).

`parseBody` on a plain `Request` (e.g. `src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:93`) also takes the buffered `arrayBuffer` -> `new Response` -> `formData` route now; nothing is retained there, but the extra transient body copy applies to every such call.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that a second `c.req.parseBody()` call, or `c.req.parseBody()` after `validator('form')`, reuses the cached `FormData` instead of parsing the body again; the only `formData` spy in `src/utils/body.test.ts` was removed by this change.

findings.title: parseBody() after c.req.formData() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts), short-circuit on the existing cache before touching arrayBuffer(), mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { /* current arrayBuffer + bufferToFormData + cache assignment */ }`. Add a request.test.ts case for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies. Verified on a scratch copy of the head sources: this restores `{ foo: 'bar' }` for both sequences and keeps the mixed-case and parseBody-then-text/cloneRawRequest results unchanged. Alternative (assumption: every supported runtime parses the media type case-insensitively, confirmed only on Node 24): revert parseFormData to `await (request as Request).formData()` and keep only the new `mediaType` gate in parseBody.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()

residual_risks: Narrowed accepted input in parseBody(): the gate changed from `contentType.startsWith(...)` to strict equality on the part before `;` (src/utils/body.ts:104-106). A comma-joined Content-Type, which is what `Headers` yields when a client or proxy sends the header twice (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), parsed to `{ foo: 'bar' }` on base and returns `{}` on head (executed probe, Node 24). Malformed input, so low priority, but it is a silent empty result rather than an error.

Hyrum's Law on the plain-`Request` path: parseBody(request) no longer calls `request.formData()`; it calls `request.arrayBuffer()` and re-parses through `new Response(...)` (src/utils/body.ts:126-127). A Request-like object or test double that overrides only `formData()` is now bypassed (probe: base returned the overridden `{custom:'yes'}`, head returned the wire body). The diff itself had to rewrite body.test.ts 'should not update file object properties' because its `vi.spyOn(req, 'formData')` mock stopped being consulted. Callsite completeness for external adapters or polyfilled Request classes: not checkable from this repo.

Observable body-cache changes after parseBody() on a form request that are improvements but still behavior changes in a patch release: `Object.keys(c.req.bodyCache)` is now `['arrayBuffer','formData']` instead of `['formData']`, so `c.req.text()` after parseBody() returns the original wire body (`foo=bar`) instead of a re-serialized multipart string, and `cloneRawRequest()` after parseBody() now yields a parseable request where base threw. `c.req.text()`/`arrayBuffer()` followed by parseBody() also now succeeds where base threw a TypeError. Verified on Node 24 only; other runtimes (Bun, Deno, workerd) were not exercised.
testing_gaps: No test covers `await c.req.formData()` followed by `await c.req.parseBody()` on the same HonoRequest (multipart and urlencoded); this is the sequence that regresses and src/request.test.ts:367-430 only exercises parseBody() first.

No test pins parseBody() after another cached body read (`text()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `blob()`) or after `validator('form')`, so the new arrayBuffer-based path through HonoRequest's body cache has no regression coverage beyond the direct mixed-case cases.

findings.title: c.req.formData() then c.req.parseBody() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts:121-139) restore `const formData = await (request as Request).formData()` and drop the arrayBuffer/bufferToFormData/bodyCache lines; the new media-type check in `parseBody` alone satisfies the issue, because native `Request.formData()` parses `Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=...` and `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` case-insensitively (verified on Node 24; assumption: other runtimes follow the same WHATWG MIME parsing). If the arrayBuffer path is kept deliberately, first reuse an existing cache entry, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { ...arrayBuffer path... }`. Either way add a HonoRequest regression test for `await req.formData(); await req.parseBody()` with both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: `parseBody(request)` no longer calls `request.formData()` on the object it is given (probe: a Request whose `formData` is overridden is ignored on head, used on base; the diff also had to delete the `vi.spyOn(req, 'formData')` mock in src/utils/body.test.ts). Callers of the public `hono/utils/body` export that pass Request-like objects or runtime Requests with their own `formData` implementation now go through `arrayBuffer()` plus a synthetic `Response` instead; only Node was exercised here.

After `c.req.parseBody()` the request now keeps both the full raw body (`bodyCache.arrayBuffer`) and the parsed FormData for its lifetime (probe: cache keys are `arrayBuffer,formData` on head, `formData` on base), so file uploads are held roughly twice in memory. Not measured against bodyLimit or large uploads.
